newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa white maize prices rise on heavy exports.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa white maize prices rise on heavy exports.

text.p: Prices for South African white maize are being pumped up as the crop, rolling in after a rain-delayed harvest, is whisked off the land and railed to the coast to fill export commitments to Kenya and South America.
But industry analysts said the shortage would be temporary as maize yields looked to be higher than expected after fears that wet and cold weather had damaged crops.
"The ships are in the harbour and traders have to get the maize down there. There is little available for the local guys," said a trader at a local commodity house.
July white contracts on the South African Futures Exchange (Safex) rose nine rand last week to finish at 597 rand a tonne. Near month yellow maize slipped five rand to 552 rand in quiet trade.
"The market is telling us that there is a shortage of white at the moment," said Rod Blondin, general manager of the agricultural markets division of Safex.
Traders said export slots had been fully booked up to the end of August.

Konrad Keyser, grain marketing manager at Sentraal Wes -- the country's largest grain co-operative -- said that between 30 and 35 percent of maize in its growing area had been harvested and that quality and yields were looking fairly robust.

"At the beginning there were some quality problems with all the rains we had. At this stage I feel that there will be a bit more (lower) Grade 2 but that will not be much of a problem. And yield-wise it looks like it is better than expected," he said.

Traders said the squeeze on white would ease off as more maize was harvested and slammed the National Maize Producers Organisation's (Nampo) statement last week that there would be shortage for the whole season.
"It is not as tight as the producers say. The final crop figure will probably be around 8.2 million tonnes, split pretty equally between white and yellow," one trader said.

The trader added that based on an 8.2 million tonne estimate some 650,000 tonnes of white maize would still be available at the end of the season after taking into account exports, consumption and carryover.
South Africa's official forecast, which is updated monthly, estimates a harvest of 7.966 million tonnes, which is nearly two million tonnes above consumption.

Nampo said last week that even if the crop estimate was 10 to 15 percent higher, white maize would still be in short supply. They said the current situation was exacerbated by export commitments currently of some 1.3 million tonnes of mostly white maize.

Traders said the early build up of El Nino, a weather phenomenon which has previously caused devastating drought in southern African, was being talked about in the market but had not yet made an impact on prices.
"We will only know nearer December whether El Nino will hit. People will maybe start stocking up with maize closer to that time, but right now it's just talk," one said.
Safex's Blondin said the last trading day for July contracts would be Tuesday. A contract for July 1998 is to be listed on August 1, he said.
